new_statements.rule_in_words: Across the Aru languages (East Tarangan included, per the marked forms in the tables), stress is by default on the penultimate syllable, but falls on the final syllable when that syllable contains a mid vowel; words deviating from this default are individually marked with an acute accent in the data (e.g. NE/SE Tarangan maŋár 'sky', East Tarangan ɔnít 'flying fox' with unexpected final stress).
new_statements.exceptions: Lexical exceptions exist and are marked item-by-item with an acute accent ('unexpected stress'); East Tarangan examples in the book include maŋár 'sky' and ɔnít 'flying fox' (final stress without a final mid vowel).
new_statements.domain_note: A transcription default for citation forms (mostly roots) in a comparative database covering all 14 Aru languages; not an East-Tarangan-specific analysis; word vs. root domain and behaviour under affixation are not addressed (for the sister language West Tarangan, Nivens 1992/2002 states the same rule over the root).
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement found is an Aru-family-wide transcription default (all Aru languages in Nivens' 2017 Proto-Aru database, as restated by Grimes & Edwards 2026), not a description of East Tarangan (east2465) specifically; it is applied to East Tarangan forms in their tables (Northeast Tarangan = Gomar Meti/Fatlabata villages, Southeast Tarangan = Dosi Mar/Salarem/Beltubur villages), where deviating forms carry an acute accent (e.g. NE/SE Tarangan maŋár 'sky', East Tarangan ɔnít 'flying fox'). Note that the Pusat Bahasa volume 'Sintaksis bahasa Tarangan' (1995) uses 'Tarangan Timur' for Karey (kare1338), a different language; the sister language West Tarangan (west2538) is already in the catalog from Nivens 1992.
